usage: This is the most common, versatile way to say 'hello' across the Levant. It is appropriate for both formal and informal situations, regardless of the gender or number of people being addressed. In Lebanon and affluent urban areas, you will also frequently hear 'hi' or 'bonjour', but 'mar7aba' remains universally understood and used.

variants.label: warm / enthusiastic
variants.note: Used to show enthusiasm when greeting someone, especially common in Jordan and Palestine.

variants.label: formal / traditional
variants.note: Used in more formal, traditional, or religious contexts, often when entering a shop or joining a group.

variants.label: casual / modern
variants.note: Borrowed from English, this is extremely common among younger people and in urban centers like Beirut or Amman.
